classification.difficultyReason: Find an adjacent angle on a straight line, then apply the alternate segment theorem.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: An inscribed triangle and horizontal tangent at its bottom vertex. Distinct arcs show the 130-degree angle from the rightward tangent to the upper-left chord and the adjacent unknown x between that chord and the leftward tangent. The opposite triangle angle is y. Decorative source colours are replaced with ordinary black geometry.
spec.mathematics: The tangent touches the circle at the bottom vertex. The adjacent tangent angles sum to 180 degrees; the alternate segment theorem makes y equal to x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only x, y and the given 130-degree angle appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+130^\circ&=180^\circ\\x&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
By the alternate segment theorem,
$$y=50^\circ.$$
